items.source_operations: The source uses addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by sample size, finite sums, absolute value, expectation, argmax, and strict or weak inequalities as appropriate to this item.
items.lean_operations: The elaborated Lean atoms use the same real operations, finite sums or PMF expectations, absolute values, maxima, and strictness direction after paper definitions are expanded.
items.source_coercions: Finite counts and class or sample cardinalities enter real-valued averages through the ordinary natural-to-real embedding; posterior scores and weights remain real-valued.
items.lean_coercions: Lean embeds natural counts and finite cardinalities into the reals before division and otherwise retains the source real-valued arithmetic domain.
items.source_division: Accuracy, marginal shares, and aggregate posteriors divide by the positive source sample size N; simplex and positive-sample hypotheses provide the stated domain.
items.lean_division: Lean uses real division by the same finite sample cardinality or natural sample size and exposes positivity where a theorem relies on cancellation.
items.source_rounding: None of these reviewed mathematical statements performs floor, ceiling, integer truncation, or numerical approximation.
items.lean_rounding: The reviewed Lean atoms perform no floor, ceiling, integer truncation, or approximate arithmetic operation.
items.source_normalization: Empirical shares and posterior aggregates normalize by N; posterior and reference vectors and all PMF laws have unit mass.
items.lean_normalization: The same finite-sample and unit-mass normalizations are visible in the expanded definitions and theorem conclusions.
items.source_strictness: The source distinguishes weak argmax and optimality comparisons from strict one-row improvements and the strict weight condition gamma below one.
items.lean_strictness: Lean preserves the source weak or strict comparison in every reviewed conclusion and explicit premise.
items.source_zero_denominator: The source's N>K and positive-sample conditions ensure that every claimed 1/N normalization and P_N^q lower bound is meaningful.
items.lean_zero_denominator: Lean exposes positive sample-size hypotheses or finite nonempty carriers wherever the proof requires division or an argmax witness.
items.relation_basis: After the ordinary finite-count-to-real embedding, every exposed arithmetic operation, normalization, expectation, and inequality direction is the source formula itself or a proved algebraically identical expansion.

items.relation_basis: After ordinary finite-count-to-real coercions and recursive expansion of the paper-local definitions, every reviewed equality, expectation, normalization, objective comparison, and strictness direction is the cited source formula or its direct logical implication.

numeric_semantics_review.absence_basis: No manifest-visible arithmetic operation occurs in the obligations classified as nonnumeric.

discrete_semantics_review.absence_basis: The elaborated signature contains no order-sensitive list-prefix, first-occurrence, duplicate-sensitive completion, or related discrete sequence operator; fixed-order argmax is represented propositionally, not by a reviewed list algorithm.

algorithm_review.source_claim_basis: The cited item is a mathematical bias identity or an expected-policy optimality necessity theorem and makes no executable-runner or complexity claim.
algorithm_review.lean_claim_basis: The Lean declaration exposes and proves the corresponding proposition but does not claim an implementation, stopping behavior, or runtime bound.

semantic_worlds.semantics: Source and Lean use the same finite classification model, probability laws, fixed tie-breaking, positive-support meaning, dataset-indexed reference family, expected objectives, and almost-sure agreement conclusion applicable to this row.

output_shape.source_semantics: For the exact dataset-dependent P_N^q reference family and 0 <= gamma < 1, every independent rule that maximizes O_N^gamma agrees with argmax almost surely.
output_shape.lean_semantics: The full expanded conclusion gives the same zero-bias equality or the same implication from exact source hypotheses and expected-policy optimality to probability-one argmax agreement.
output_shape.relation_basis: The complete source endpoint is compared with the complete elaborated result atom, including the reference choice, support or P_N^q condition, expectation law, weight range, and terminal equality.
output_shape.source_output_shape: The source item has one complete universal implication terminating in a zero-bias identity or almost-sure argmax-agreement claim.
output_shape.lean_output_shape: The Lean result atom has the same complete implication and terminal real equality, with no projected coordinate or omitted conjunct.
output_shape.projection_terminal_policy: No support condition, dataset dependence, expected accuracy or fidelity component, objective maximality premise, gamma bound, or terminal probability equality is omitted.
output_shape.arity_basis: Every elaborated binder and the full result atom are audited against the pinned theorem and proof locators, not against a selected theorem name or abbreviated projection.
output_shape.lean_evidence_statement: The elaborated result exposes the complete source-facing proposition and the theorem evidence proves it without a certificate, external constructor, or caller-supplied conclusion package.

adversarial_action_space.absence_basis: This classification-policy theorem does not quantify unilateral reports, reorderings, completions, or another adversarial transformation carrier whose emptiness could make the claim vacuous.

coherent_extrema_witness.absence_basis: The result does not combine separately selected coordinatewise extrema; every argmax and policy comparison uses one coherent rule or dataset policy witness.

cardinality_fibers.absence_basis: The result makes no equality between a syntactic family cardinality and nonempty realized semantic fibers and invokes no surjective counting identity.

execution_claim_scope.absence_basis: The result is a mathematical identity or optimality implication and makes no executable-runner, stopping-time, or complexity claim.
